sections.DESCRIPTION:
You do not believe that the divine must remain mysterious.
Where priests approach sacred power through devotion, revelation and service, you approach it through study. To you, prayers are more than acts of worship: they are structures of language, intent and spiritual authority that can be recorded, compared, reconstructed and understood.
Your education may have taken place within a great temple archive, an isolated monastery, a university devoted to comparative theology or beneath the suspicious eye of a single ageing scholar. You may be an orthodox theologian faithfully preserving the traditions of your religion, or a radical researcher who believes that no church has the right to decide which sacred knowledge should survive.
Your most valuable possession is your Prayer Book. Its pages contain prayers copied from temple records, fragments recovered from ruined shrines, instructions for forgotten rites, translations of ancient scripture and notes written in your own hand. Two Archivists studying the same religion may possess entirely different collections.
Unlike a Cleric, your Divinity magic does not require devotion to a particular deity or Divine Aspect. You may be deeply religious, sceptical, devoted to several traditions or fascinated by religion without personally worshipping anything at all. Your ability to cast Divinity spells represents your understanding of the structures through which sacred power is invoked, rather than an automatic reward for obedience.
Archivists are at their strongest when given time to prepare. Their Prayer Books can eventually contain an enormous selection of magic, while their ability to consult and reinterpret those texts allows them to adjust their prepared spells when circumstances change.
You may want to play an Archivist if you enjoy learned spellcasting, collecting spells, religious scholarship, deciphering forgotten knowledge and preparing the correct answer to a problem before everybody else has realised there is a problem.
An Archivist does not ask whether a prayer is true. An Archivist asks who wrote it, what it does, what was removed from the surviving copy, and why.
sections.PROFICIENCIES: You are not proficient in any armour. You are proficient with the club, dagger and staff.
sections.CLASS SKILLS: Artistry, Culture, Linguistics, Medicine, Meditation, Mental Focus, Occultism, Planes, Power Manipulation, Religion and Sense Motive.
sections.CLASS ABILITIES: You gain the following abilities as an Archivist as you advance in levels.
sections.ARCHIVIST'S PRAYER BOOK:
Your Prayer Book is a scholarly collection of sacred formulae, liturgies, invocations, reconstructed prayers and theological annotations.
At 1st level, select six PP 2 spells from the Divinity tradition and record them within your Prayer Book.
Each time you gain an Archivist level, you may add two additional Divinity spells to your Prayer Book. These spells must have a PP cost that you are capable of casting.
You may learn additional Divinity spells encountered during play using the normal rules for learning and copying spells. Sacred scrolls, another Archivist's Prayer Book, temple manuscripts and similar written sources may therefore substantially expand your collection.
Your Prayer Book may contain prayers belonging to religions other than your own. Recording a prayer does not mean that you accept the beliefs contained within it.
Specialist spells cannot be learned merely by copying them into your Prayer Book. They continue to require the appropriate class ability, feat or other source granting access, as normal under the Specialist Spell rules.
sections.SCHOLARLY EXEGESIS:
You have been trained to approach religion as a discipline of investigation rather than relying entirely upon intuition or faith.
When you make a Religion check to Recall Knowledge, identify a Divinity spell or magical effect, interpret religious doctrine, recognise sacred symbolism, study a religious rite or understand a sacred text, you may use Intelligence in place of the ability score normally associated with that check.
This does not change the ability score used for unrelated Religion actions where academic knowledge is irrelevant.
sections.RECITE FROM THE TEXT:
CONCENTRATE FOCUS
Action 1 AP
Requirements You have your Prayer Book available and are able to read or otherwise consult it.
You rapidly locate a familiar passage, annotation or alternative formulation before invoking a prepared prayer.
Select one Divinity spell that you do not currently have memorised, but which is recorded in your Prayer Book. You may cast this spell immediately (using its normal AP cost). If the spell is not cast before the end of your turn, the ability is wasted.
sections.BONUS FEATS: At 1st level, you gain Heighten Spell, Scribe Scroll and Spell Substitution as granted feats. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, you may select an additional class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or possess an appropriate class trait for the selected feat.
sections.DEIFIC ASPECTS:
An Archivist does not automatically select a deity or Divine Aspect. You may worship any deity or follow any Divine Aspect appropriate to your character, but this belief is separate from your Archivist spellcasting unless another ability specifically connects the two.
If another feat, archetype or class ability grants you a Divine Aspect, you gain whatever benefits that rule specifies normally. Merely possessing a written copy of a Divine Aspect's Specialist Spell does not allow you to cast that spell.
sections.MAGICAL TRADITION:
You are a learned Divinity spellcaster. Unlike a Cleric, you do not have access to the entire Divinity spell list during daily preparation. You may memorise only spells contained within your Prayer Book.
During your daily preparation, you spend approximately 30 minutes studying, reciting and mentally reconstructing the prayers contained within your book.
At the end of this time, you may memorise an amount of spells for which you meet the casting requirements equal to 2 + (Archivist level x 2). You select these spells from those recorded in your Prayer Book.
sections.CANTRIPS: Each day when you prepare your spells, you may also memorise any four Divinity cantrips. Cantrips do not need to be recorded within your Prayer Book, and you may change your selected cantrips during each daily preparation.
sections.MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE: Intelligence is your magical ability score. You add your Intelligence modifier to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your Power Points.
sections.SPECIALIST SPELLS: Your Archival Discipline grants you a unique Specialist Spell at 1st level and another at 7th level. You may select additional specialist spells from those available to the Cleric class by selecting the Specialist Spell Class feat.
sections.CONTROL LEVELS: For the purposes of calculating Control Levels, the Archivist gains +1 Control Level per Archivist level.
sections.ARCHIVAL DISCIPLINE:
At 1st level, you select an Archival Discipline representing the branch of sacred scholarship in which you received your most intensive training.
Your Archival Discipline grants you a Specialist Skill, a 1st-level Specialist Spell, a unique Discipline Ability and an Advanced Specialist Spell at 7th level.
The five Archival Disciplines are Canonist, Apocryphist, Eschatologist, Hagiographer and Revelator.
sections.CANONIST:
You specialise in authorised scripture, ecclesiastical law and the formal doctrines through which organised religions define themselves. Canonists are frequently employed by great temples to settle questions of doctrine, authenticate official texts and identify deviations from established teachings. Others become critics of those same institutions because nobody is better equipped to expose a church breaking its own rules than someone who knows exactly what those rules say.
Specialist Skill Canon Lore
Specialist Spells Doctrinal Ward (1), Word of Censure (7)
Authoritative Interpretation: When you successfully Recall Knowledge about a religion, Divine Aspect, divine servant or Divinity spell or effect using Religion or Canon Lore, you gain a +1-status bonus to your next saving throw against that creature or effect before the end of your next turn. You may instead grant this bonus to one ally within 30 feet who can hear and understand you.
sections.APOCRYPHIST:
You study the texts that others tried to destroy. Suppressed gospels, forbidden prayers, contradictory accounts of miracles and scriptures declared heretical all fall within your field. You do not necessarily believe these writings, but you understand that destroyed information is frequently the information somebody most feared being remembered.
Specialist Skill Heresy Lore
Specialist Spells Hidden Doctrine (1), Forbidden Name (7)
Forbidden Research: You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to checks made to identify or understand curses, corrupted Divinity magic, religious heresies, forbidden divine rites and deliberately concealed alterations to sacred texts. In addition, you gain a +1-circumstance bonus to Counteract checks against effects with either the Curse or Soul trait when you have successfully identified the effect.
sections.ESCHATOLOGIST:
Your studies concern mortality and everything claimed to lie beyond it. You compare funerary texts, accounts of resurrection, descriptions of the afterlife and testimony concerning souls, ghosts and undeath. Few Archivists possess a more detailed understanding of what cultures believe happens when the heart stops beating - and fewer still are comfortable with how often those beliefs contradict observable evidence.
Specialist Skill Soul Lore
Specialist Spells Last Rite (1), Anchor the Departing Soul (7)
Scholar of the Last Road: You gain a +1-class bonus to saving throws against Soul Drain, possession and effects with the Soul trait. You also gain advantage when attempting to Recall Knowledge about Undead, Unliving creatures, souls and effects concerned directly with death or resurrection.
sections.HAGIOGRAPHER:
You specialise in the lives and deeds of those believed to have touched the divine directly: saints, prophets, chosen champions, divine servants, avatars and the Eternals. Hagiographers compare miraculous accounts against historical evidence, track relics, reconstruct lost pilgrimages and attempt to distinguish genuine intervention from centuries of exaggeration.
Specialist Skill Eternal Lore
Specialist Spells Exemplar's Grace (1), Saintly Intercession (7)
Lives of the Exemplars: You gain Advantage on Recall Knowledge checks concerning Eternals, divine servants, avatars, saints, sacred relics and historically recorded miracles. When you successfully identify such a creature, you may also ask for one piece of information concerning its known religious significance, traditional behaviour or recorded weaknesses as part of the same check.
sections.REVELATOR:
You study prophecy, visions, omens and religious experiences in which knowledge appears to arrive without any identifiable mortal source. Rather than accepting every revelation at face value, you compare patterns across centuries of prophetic records. A genuine vision, a hallucination, deliberate fraud and supernatural manipulation can all look remarkably similar to somebody who desperately wants to believe.
Specialist Skill Prophecy Lore
Specialist Spells Read Omen (1), Unfold the Future (7)
Calculated Portent: During your daily preparation, select Fortitude, Reflex or Will. Once before your next daily preparation, when you or an ally within 30 feet attempts the selected saving throw, you may use a Reaction to grant that creature advantage to the saving throw. You must declare the use of Calculated Portent before the result of the saving throw is resolved. Once used, the portent is expended.

sections.DESCRIPTION:
The oldest protections were not written in spellbooks.
They were tied above doors with red thread, buried beneath hearthstones, whispered over the newly dead and brewed into bitter tea by people who could not always explain why the recipe worked, only that it had been passed down for generations.
You are a Folkwarden, a keeper of the practical traditions through which ordinary people have survived alongside the supernatural. Your knowledge lies somewhere between medicine, folklore, natural philosophy and magic. You know which herbs genuinely reduce fever, and which are merely traditional; which changes in birdsong warn of a predator and which suggest that something unnatural has entered the woods; why certain villages nail iron above their doors; and how a body should be prepared so that nothing unwelcome finds an empty home waiting for it.
Not every folk belief is true. You have simply become very good at discovering which ones are.
Folkwardens are found wherever formal priests, physicians or magical orders are distant, expensive or mistrusted. They may serve as herbalists, midwives, charm-makers, corpse tenders, weather readers, counsellors and guardians of local custom. Some learn within a long family tradition, while others are apprenticed to a single village elder or collect fragments of the Old Ways while travelling from settlement to settlement.
Your Verdant magic grows from this practical relationship with the living world. Unlike a Druid, you are not wholly devoted to mastering nature, and unlike a Shaman you do not rely upon direct communion with spirits. Your spellcasting is a smaller body of instinctive workings reinforced by experience, repetition and an understanding of the rhythms that connect living creatures, places and communities.
In an adventuring party, you are strongest when given time to prepare. You make dangerous places safer, recognise when the natural world has been disturbed, prepare remedies before afflictions become deadly and protect companions against threats that cannot always be stopped with armour.
You may want to play a Folkwarden if you enjoy practical support, folklore, exploration, medicine, protective rites and using skills to solve supernatural problems before magic becomes necessary.
A priest knows the prayer. A wizard knows the spell. A Folkwarden knows why nobody in this village opens that window after sunset.
sections.PROFICIENCIES: You are proficient with light armour and shields, except tower shields. You are proficient with all simple weapons, as well as the spear and shortbow.
sections.CLASS SKILLS: Artistry, Culture, Crafting, Diplomacy, Handle Animal, Linguistics, Medicine, Meditation, Mental Focus, Nature, Occultism, Perception, Power Manipulation, Religion, Sense Motive and Survival.
sections.CLASS ABILITIES: You gain the following abilities as a Folkwarden as you advance in levels.
sections.FOLK ALCHEMY:
At 1st level, your knowledge of herbs, minerals, resins, extracts and traditional remedies extends naturally into the practical science of alchemy.
You gain the Alchemist archetype feat as a bonus feat. You do not expend a class feat pick to gain this archetype and may gain it even if you do not meet its normal prerequisites.
You gain all of the normal benefits of the Alchemist archetype, including the Alchemical Crafting feat and proficiency with alchemical weapons. Crafting is already a Folkwarden class skill and therefore gaining it as a class skill again provides no additional benefit.
The Alchemist archetype gained through Folk Alchemy does not impose its normal Progression Requirements upon you. You are not required to attain Crafting +10 ranks before selecting another archetype feat.
sections.KEEPER OF THE OLD WAYS:
You gain Folk Lore as a specialist skill.
Folk Lore covers local superstition, protective customs, traditional remedies, household rites, burial practices, taboos, omens and the ways ordinary communities understand supernatural events.
You may use Folk Lore in place of Culture, Nature, Religion or Occultism when the check specifically concerns a folk practice, traditional remedy, omen, superstition, local taboo or customary protection. Folk Lore does not replace those skills for their broader uses. You might use Folk Lore to recognise why thorn branches have been tied above every doorway in a village, but not to identify an unrelated Arcane spell simply because the villagers are frightened of it.
Be aware that Folk Lore is unique to this class and cannot be selected as specialist skill by any other class.
sections.PRACTICAL COUNSEL:
At 2nd level, your experience allows you to help others through explanation, diagnosis, preparation and warning rather than simply performing a task yourself.
Whenever you use Aid in this way, you may make the Aid check using any appropriate Folkwarden class skill, Folk Lore or one of your Folk Tradition specialist skills instead of the skill normally required, provided that your knowledge can reasonably contribute to the task.
If you achieve at least a Success on the Aid check, increase the circumstance bonus granted by 1, to a maximum of +4. This does not change the AP cost, DC or other normal rules for Aid.
If your assistance is verbal, the recipient must be able to hear and understand you. Practical Counsel does not remove physical requirements that are essential to performing the task and cannot be used to replace an attack roll when using Aid Offensive or Aid Defensive.
sections.SEASONED HANDS:
At 3rd level, experience has taught you to recognise a dangerous mistake before you commit to it.
Whenever you Fumble a Folk Lore check, a check made as part of Read the Signs or Lay to Rest, or a Medicine check made to Treat Disease, Treat Toxin or Treat Wounds, treat the result as a Failure instead. You gain no information or benefit from the failed check but avoid the additional consequences of the Fumble.
Furthermore, when treating a non-magical Disease or Poison originating from a natural plant, animal, fungus or environmental substance, you may use Nature instead of Medicine for the check. This does not apply to manufactured alchemical toxins, supernatural afflictions or other substances that your knowledge of the natural world would not reasonably cover.
sections.BONUS FEATS:
At 1st level, you gain Heighten Spell as a bonus feat.
At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, you gain an additional class feat. You must meet its prerequisites or possess the appropriate Folkwarden, Adept or Expert trait.
You therefore gain bonus class feats at 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level.
sections.MAGICAL TRADITION:
You are a verdant instinctive spell caster. Your key stat for spell casting is Constitution, and you select your Spell Lists from the Verdant Tradition.
At 1st level, select two PP 2 Verdant spells and add them to your repertoire. At 3rd level and every two levels thereafter (5th, 7th, 9th and so forth), select one additional Verdant spell that you are capable of casting and add it to your repertoire.
You may cast these spells whenever you meet their casting requirements and possess sufficient PP.
At 5th level and every two levels thereafter, you may replace one spell in your repertoire with another Verdant spell that you are capable of casting.
sections.CANTRIPS: At 1st level, select two Verdant cantrips. These become part of your permanent repertoire and do not need to be memorised.
sections.MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE: Constitution is your magical ability score. You add your Constitution modifier to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your Power Points.
sections.SPECIALIST SPELLS:
At 1st level, you gain one PP 1 Folkwarden Specialist Spell of your choice.
Folkwarden Specialist Spells are presented in Chapter 9 and concentrate on charms, remedies, wards, omens and practical Verdant workings.
Additional Folkwarden Specialist Spells may be learned through the normal Specialist Spell feat and Folkwarden class feats.
sections.FOLK RITES:
At 1st level, you learn the practical rites common to Folkwardens. Folk Rites are class abilities rather than spells. They are performed through learned procedure, appropriate materials and a limited amount of Verdant power.
Unless a rite states otherwise, ordinary components such as herbs, cord, wax, salt, chalk, carved wood, feathers, stones, nails or incense have negligible cost. A Folk Rite possessing the Verdant trait is magical and interacts normally with effects that detect, suppress or Counteract magic. Folk Rites are explained in detail below
sections.FOLK PREPARATIONS:
Some Folk Rites create Preparations. You may maintain a number of active Preparations equal to your Folkwarden class bonus.
Warding Charm, Brew Remedy and Ward the Threshold create Preparations. Read the Signs and Lay to Rest do not count against this limit.
If creating a new Preparation would exceed your limit, select one of your existing Preparations. That Preparation immediately becomes ineffective. Unless otherwise stated, a Preparation remains effective until used, destroyed or your next daily preparation.
A creature cannot benefit from two copies of the same Preparation created by you at the same time. Preparations created by different Folkwardens follow the normal rules for bonuses of the same type and do not automatically stack. Preparations cannot be sold as permanent magical or alchemical items. When a rule requires a Counteract level for one of your magical Folk Rites or Preparations, use your Folkwarden level.
sections.WARDING CHARM:
CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE VERDANT WARDING
Action 10 minutes
You fashion a small protective charm from appropriate materials: a knotted cord, carved token, herb bundle, inscribed stone, nail, feather or similar object.
Choose one of the following protections when you create the charm:
Mind Fear effects, effects with the Mental trait and supernatural Sleep effects.
Soul Possession, Soul Drain and effects with the Soul trait.
Hex Effects with the Curse trait.
The charm becomes one of your active Preparations. A creature carrying the charm may activate it as a Reaction immediately before attempting an eligible saving throw. The creature gains a circumstance bonus to the triggering saving throw equal to half your Folkwarden class bonus (round up). The charm is then expended.
sections.BREW REMEDY:
MANIPULATE
Action 10 minutes
Requirements You possess healer's tools, suitable herbs or comparable materials.
You prepare a medicinal draught, powdered herb mixture, poultice or other traditional remedy. Choose Disease or Poison when creating the remedy.
The remedy becomes one of your active Preparations. A creature may consume or apply the remedy as an Interact action (1 AP). For 1 hour, the creature gains a circumstance bonus to saving throws against the chosen type of affliction equal to half your Folkwarden class bonus (round up). If the creature is already afflicted, this bonus applies to eligible saving throws made against that affliction during the duration.
The Preparation ends when consumed or applied. Brew Remedy is not magical healing and does not automatically remove an affliction.
sections.WARD THE THRESHOLD:
CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE VERDANT WARDING
Action 10 minutes
Area 10-foot emanation centred upon a fixed point
You mark a room, campsite, doorway, shrine or similar location using a ring or pattern of traditional wards. The ward becomes one of your active Preparations.
Willing creatures within the area gain a circumstance bonus equal to half your Folkwarden class bonus (round up) to saving throws against Fear, possession, Soul Drain and effects with the Soul trait.
A creature resting or sleeping within the ward also gains this bonus against supernatural Sleep effects and magical effects attempting to influence its mind or soul while it rests.
Ward the Threshold does not prevent creatures from physically entering the area, reveal hidden creatures or identify supernatural threats. Moving or deliberately destroying the objects that form the ward ends the Preparation.
sections.READ THE SIGNS:
CONCENTRATE INVESTIGATION
Action 10 minutes
You study the subtle signs within your surroundings: tracks, disturbed vegetation, insect behaviour, birdsong, weather, smoke, water, fungal growth, animal remains, unusual silence and countless other details.
Make a Nature or Survival check against a DC determined by the GM, normally the Area Level DC modified by the age and obscurity of the signs.
Heroic You may ask four questions.
Critical You may ask three questions.
Success You may ask two questions.
Partial You may ask one question.
Failure You cannot draw a reliable conclusion.
Fumble You misunderstand the signs. The GM may provide one plausible but incorrect conclusion.
Appropriate questions include what significant creature or group passed through the area recently, the general direction in which it travelled, what natural hazard presents the greatest immediate danger, whether the local environment is behaving unnaturally, whether a significant supernatural disturbance has affected the area, or where the nearest likely source of shelter, fresh water or another ordinary natural resource can be found.
The GM may permit other questions where appropriate. Read the Signs cannot reveal information that has left no physical, behavioural or environmental trace.
sections.LAY TO REST:
CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE SOUL VERDANT WARDING
Action 10 minutes
Target One corpse or collection of substantially complete remains
You prepare the dead according to traditional funerary practices intended to protect the remains from necromantic misuse, possession and other violations of the natural passage between life and death.
Make a Medicine, Nature or Religion check against the deceased creature's Level DC. The GM determines an appropriate DC where the creature's level is unknown.
Heroic The remains are protected for 1 year.
Critical The remains are protected for 1 month.
Success The remains are protected for 1 week.
Partial The remains are protected for 24 hours.
Failure The rite provides no protection.
Fumble Something has been incorrectly prepared. You cannot attempt Lay to Rest upon those remains again until your next daily preparation.
While protected, an effect attempting to animate the remains as an Undead creature, possess the remains or bind another soul into them must first successfully Counteract your Lay to Rest.
Lay to Rest does not prevent ordinary decomposition, prevent communication with the dead, prevent resurrection, compel a departed soul to remain or depart, destroy an existing Undead creature or affect an Undead creature that has already been created from the remains.
sections.FOLK TRADITION:
At 1st level, select one Folk Tradition. Your Tradition represents the area of folk practice in which your training is strongest. Choose Charmwright, Gravetender, Hearthkeeper, Herbal or Omen Reader.
Each Tradition grants a specialist skill and a Tradition Ability. Later Folkwarden class feats may develop your chosen Tradition further.
sections.CHARMWRIGHT:
You specialise in knots, carved tokens, herb bundles and other portable protections.
Specialist Skill Charm Lore
Many-Layered Charm Whenever you create a Warding Charm, select two of its protection categories instead of one. The charm is still expended after it is activated once, regardless of which protection triggered it.
sections.GRAVETENDER:
You learned the customs surrounding death long before you learned to fear the dead themselves.
Specialist Skill Burial Lore
Quiet Passage You gain a +2-class bonus to checks made as part of Lay to Rest. Furthermore, increase the duration of a successful Lay to Rest by one step: Partial becomes 1 week, Success becomes 1 month, Critical becomes 1 year and Heroic remains effective until the remains are deliberately desecrated, destroyed or the rite is successfully Counteracted.
sections.HEARTHKEEPER:
You specialise in protecting homes, families, camps and the places in which people gather.
Specialist Skill Hearth Lore
Safe Hearth The radius of your Ward the Threshold increases from 10 feet to 20 feet. When warding a single ordinary room of comparable size, you may instead shape the ward around the room boundaries rather than using an exact emanation.
sections.HERBAL:
You understand that the difference between medicine and poison is frequently a matter of quantity, timing and preparation.
Specialist Skill Herbalism Lore
Deep Stores Whenever you use Brew Remedy, you create two doses of the same remedy. The two doses collectively count as only one active Preparation. The Preparation ends when both doses have been consumed, applied or destroyed.
sections.OMEN READER:
You have been taught to listen when the living world warns you.
Specialist Skill Omen Lore
Clear Signs You gain a +2-class bonus to checks made as part of Read the Signs. On a Heroic, Critical or Success result, you may ask one additional question.

sections.DESCRIPTION:
You have been taught that faith requires more than prayer. There are things that hide behind scripture, wear familiar faces and speak sacred words while corrupting everything those words were meant to protect. Possessing spirits whisper through unwilling mouths. Necromancers bind souls that should have passed beyond mortal reach. False prophets manufacture miracles. Cursed relics lie beneath temple altars, and sometimes the greatest threat to a faith is found within its own hierarchy.
You are trained to find these things.
Grimwards are investigators, interrogators and hunters employed by temples, sacred orders and independent religious authorities to uncover supernatural corruption. Some are solemn exorcists who would rather save a possessed victim than destroy them. Others are relentless witch-hunters, doctrinal investigators or wandering judges who believe that no institution - including their own - is above examination.
You combine practical investigative training with limited Divinity magic and enough martial skill to survive when an inquiry becomes violent. You are not a Crusader. A Crusader stands openly before an enemy and challenges them through strength, conviction and divine favour. You watch first. You ask questions. You examine the body, read the ward, speak to the witnesses, identify the thing wearing the priest's face - and only then do you draw your weapon.
Your greatest strength is Inquisition. By concentrating upon a particular creature, you can gather information, identify patterns and eventually place that creature under Judgement. Once you understand your enemy, you become considerably more dangerous to them.
You may want to play a Grimward if you enjoy investigation, monster hunting, interrogation, limited divine magic and turning knowledge about a specific enemy into combat advantage.
A Grimward does not burn someone because they are accused of heresy. A competent Grimward first determines whether there was ever any heresy at all.
sections.PROFICIENCIES: You are proficient in light and medium armour and shields, except tower shields. You are proficient with all simple and martial weapons.
sections.CLASS SKILLS: Athletics, Culture, Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Linguistics, Medicine, Mental Focus, Occultism, Perception, Religion, Sense Motive, Stealth and Survival.
sections.CLASS ABILITIES: You gain the following abilities as a Grimward as you advance in levels.
sections.INQUISITION:
CONCENTRATE
Action 1 AP
Requirements You can see or hear the creature, are currently tracking it, or the creature is one of your Studied Targets.
You designate one creature as the Subject of your Inquisition.
You may have only one Subject of Inquisition at a time. If you designate another creature, your previous Inquisition immediately ends. Your Subject does not need to be present. A Grimward may therefore begin an Inquisition against a creature identified through records, testimony, physical evidence or previous investigation.
Your Inquisition remains upon the creature until you select another Subject, the creature dies or you voluntarily end the Inquisition.
You add your class bonus to checks specifically made to investigate your Subject using the following actions or purposes:
• Detect Deception.
• Identify Magic affecting or created by the Subject.
• Recall Knowledge concerning the Subject.
• Research concerning the Subject.
• Search for evidence directly connected to the Subject.
• Sense Motive.
• Study Target.
• Track.
• Checks to identify curses, possession, supernatural abilities or magical effects created by the Subject.
The GM determines whether a check is sufficiently connected to the Subject to receive this bonus. Inquisition does not tell you whether the Subject is guilty, evil, corrupted or even suspicious.
sections.JUDGEMENT:
Evidence is more dangerous than suspicion.
When you achieve at least a Success on Detect Deception, Identify Magic, Recall Knowledge, a check made to identify one of your Subject's supernatural abilities, or a check made to recognise possession, corruption, a curse or transformation affecting your Subject, you may place the Subject under Judgement.
The creature remains Judged for as long as it remains your Subject of Inquisition. Against your Judged Subject:
• You gain a +1-circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the Subject.
• You gain a +1-circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects created by the Subject.
• Once per round, the first time you successfully inflict HP damage upon the Subject with a Strike or Grimward spell, you inflict +1d6 secondary damage.
• This additional damage increases to 2d6 at 9th level and 3d6 at 17th level.
The additional damage is of the same type as the triggering attack unless another Grimward ability or feat changes it.
sections.RECONSTRUCT TARGET:
INVESTIGATION
You are trained to reconstruct the identity of a creature from the traces it leaves behind. When using the Study Target action, you do not need to be able to see or directly observe a creature. Instead, you may Study a creature by examining sufficient evidence that can reasonably be attributed to that specific individual.
Suitable evidence might include blood, hair or other physical remains; tracks or repeated signs of passage; handwriting or a distinctive personal document; a weapon or possession strongly associated with the creature; magical residue produced by one of its abilities; remains of creatures it has attacked; several reliable witness descriptions; a detailed portrait or accurate physical representation; records describing its methods, habits or appearance; or a combination of lesser clues that together establish a specific identity.
Simply knowing a creature's name, ancestry, general description or reputation is not sufficient. The GM determines whether the available evidence is adequate.
When you Study Target in this manner, use the normal Study Target action and its normal time modifiers. The appropriate skill depends upon the evidence being examined. Common examples include Perception or Survival for physical traces, Religion for religious symbols or divine residue, Occultism or Power Manipulation for magical effects, Linguistics or Culture for documents, Sense Motive for behaviour and testimony, or an appropriate Lore or knowledge skill for creature-specific evidence.
On a Success, the creature becomes one of your normal Studied Targets, even though you have never encountered it personally. A Fumble follows the normal Study Target rules: you believe the reconstruction is correct, but something within the evidence has led you to an incorrect conclusion.
sections.PREPARED ADVERSARY:
When you roll Initiative and a creature that is both your Subject of Inquisition and one of your Studied Targets is participating in the encounter, you gain a +10-class bonus to your Initiative check.
Furthermore, you may immediately make an appropriate Recall Knowledge check against that creature as a free action. If this check achieves at least a Success, the creature is immediately placed under your Judgement. You may use Prepared Adversary only once when Initiative is first rolled.
sections.DEIFIC ASPECT:
As a Grimward, you must select a Divine Aspect representing the religious authority, sacred principle or theological tradition from which your mandate originates. Your Divine Aspect grants you the following benefits, as appropriate to the aspect selected:
• Edicts: a selection of edicts that must be followed.
• Anathema: actions or behaviours that violate your sacred responsibilities.
• Suggested Ethics: select one appropriate ethic for your character.
• Deific Skill: you gain the associated skill as a class skill.
• Specialist Spell: at 1st level, you gain one appropriate PP 1 Specialist Spell granted by your Divine Aspect.
• Bonus Spells: the bonus spells granted by your Divine Aspect are added to your Grimward repertoire and are always available once you meet their normal casting requirements.
• Favoured Weapon: you gain proficiency with your Divine Aspect's favoured weapon if you do not already possess it, and a +1-class bonus to attacks made with that weapon.
sections.SPECIALIST SPELLS: At 1st level, you gain one PP 1 Specialist Spell granted by your Divine Aspect. You may learn additional Grimward Specialist Spells through class feats presented in Chapter 5.
sections.BONUS FEATS: At 1st level, you gain one bonus class feat. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, you gain an additional class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or possess the appropriate Grimward, Expert or Adept trait for the feat.
sections.GRIM RESOLVE: At 2nd level, you gain a +2-class bonus to saving throws against fear, charm, compulsion and possession effects.
sections.SANCTIONED STRIKE: At 4th level, all weapon and unarmed attacks you make against your Judged Subject are treated as magical for the purpose of overcoming Resistance and Immunity. This does not grant the weapon a magical item bonus or any other magical weapon properties.
sections.MAGICAL TRADITION:
You are an instinctive Divinity spellcaster. Your magical training is less extensive than that of a Cleric, but Grimwards are deliberately taught a broad range of practical divine magic. An investigation may require protection from a curse one day, healing the victim of a possession the next, and destroying the creature responsible on the third. Grimward training therefore values adaptability over specialisation.
At 1st level, select any two PP 2 spells from the Divinity tradition and add them to your spell repertoire.
At 2nd level and every level thereafter, you may select one additional Divinity spell that you are capable of casting and add it to your repertoire.
You may cast these spells whenever you meet their casting requirements and do not need to memorise them.
At 5th level and every two levels thereafter, you may replace one spell in your Grimward repertoire with another eligible Divinity spell.
Spells granted by your Divine Aspect are added to your repertoire automatically and do not count against the number of Grimward spells you know.
sections.MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE: Wisdom is your magical ability score. You add your Wisdom modifier to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your Power Points.
sections.INQUISITORIAL DISCIPLINE: At 1st level, select one of the following Inquisitorial Disciplines: Exorcist, Grave Warden, Hexbreaker, Relic Warden or Truthseeker. Your discipline grants you a specialist skill and an additional ability.
sections.EXORCIST:
You specialise in entities that enter, control or displace mortal souls. Possession is rarely as simple as destroying the possessing entity. Exorcists are trained to distinguish willing communion from supernatural coercion and to preserve the host whenever possible.
Specialist Skill Spirit Lore
Soul Sentinel: You gain a +2-class bonus to saving throws against possession and effects that forcibly remove, control or displace your soul. When your Judged Subject is currently possessing another creature, your attacks and Grimward spells may treat the possessing entity as the intended target whenever the effect is capable of affecting it.
sections.GRAVE WARDEN:
You investigate those who refuse the natural boundary of death. Grave Wardens hunt necromancers, intelligent undead, corrupted burial sites and those who interfere with the proper passage of souls. Their training places particular emphasis upon recognising the differences between ordinary Undead creatures and the Unliving.
Specialist Skill Burial Lore
Consecrated Judgement: When your Judged Subject possesses the Undead or Unliving trait, the additional damage granted by Judgement may be inflicted as essence damage instead of its normal damage type. You also gain a +1-class bonus to Religion checks made to identify undead creatures or the effects responsible for creating them.
sections.HEXBREAKER:
You specialise in hostile magic: curses, compulsions, magical corruption and spells intended to conceal wrongdoing. Hexbreakers are frequently sent into situations where ordinary investigators cannot even trust what they see.
Specialist Skill Curse Lore
Break The Working: You gain a +2-class bonus to checks made to identify magical curses and effects created by your Subject of Inquisition. Furthermore, when attempting to Counteract a spell or magical effect created by your Judged Subject, you gain a +1-circumstance bonus to the Counteract check.
sections.RELIC WARDEN:
Not every threat has a heartbeat. You investigate corrupted relics, dangerous sacred objects, desecrated shrines and magical artefacts whose legends conceal more than they reveal.
Specialist Skill Relic Lore
Object Of Inquiry: You may use Inquisition against a magic item, haunt, ward, magical trap or other persistent magical effect instead of a creature. When doing so, you gain the normal Inquisition bonus to checks made to locate, identify, understand, disable or Counteract it. An object or effect cannot normally become Judged and does not receive the combat effects of Judgement unless another ability specifically allows it.
sections.TRUTHSEEKER:
Truthseekers investigate deception, false prophecy, disguised creatures and those who use magic to manufacture belief. They are often unpopular within their own religious institutions. This is generally considered evidence that they are doing their job properly.
Specialist Skill Interrogation Lore
Piercing Scrutiny: You gain Advantage on Detect Deception checks against your Subject of Inquisition. If you successfully Detect Deception from your Subject, you may immediately place it under Judgement without spending an additional action. You also gain a +1-class bonus to saving throws against illusion effects created by your Judged Subject.

sections.DESCRIPTION:
Some people learn to heal. Others are born unable to ignore suffering.
You possess an instinctive connection to the force that preserves mortal life. You may understand that power as divine grace, an expression of compassion, a sacred calling, an inherited blessing or simply something that has always existed within you. Whatever its origin, when another creature is wounded you can feel the disruption almost as keenly as if the injury were your own.
Unlike a Cleric, your power does not depend upon formal doctrine, a prayer book or service to a particular Divine Aspect. You may be deeply religious, completely secular or uncertain where your abilities originate. What defines you is not who you worship, but what you do with the power you possess.
Healers learn to recognise the difference between injury and illness, between a wounded body and a wounded soul. Their magic can close torn flesh, stabilise the dying and remove afflictions, but experienced Healers understand that preservation sometimes requires more than restoring Hit Points. Fear, poison, exhaustion, spiritual damage and supernatural corruption can kill just as surely as a blade.
Most Healers receive practical medical training alongside their supernatural abilities. A spell can save a life in seconds, but bandages, clean instruments and somebody who understands anatomy remain useful long after Power Points have been exhausted.
In battle, you rarely seek the centre of the fight. Your role is to keep companions standing, intervene when a wound would otherwise prove fatal and repair the damage that survives the encounter.
You may want to play a Healer if you want to be the party's premier restorative character, combining full spellcasting with Medicine, emergency intervention and powerful abilities that improve healing without preventing you from learning other Divinity magic.
A Healer does not ask whether someone deserves saving. There will be time for judgement when they are no longer bleeding.
sections.PROFICIENCIES: You are proficient with light armour. You are proficient with all simple weapons.
sections.CLASS SKILLS: Culture, Diplomacy, Linguistics, Medicine, Meditation, Mental Focus, Nature, Perception, Power Manipulation, Religion and Sense Motive.
sections.CLASS ABILITIES: You gain the following abilities as a Healer as you advance in levels.
sections.GIFT OF HEALING:
Healing magic responds to you with an ease that other spellcasters struggle to reproduce.
You gain a +2-class bonus to Spellcraft checks made to cast spells with the Healing trait and to Counteract checks made using such spells.
Whenever one of your spells with the Healing trait restores Hit Points to one or more creatures, and at least one recipient is a creature other than yourself, select one eligible target. That target regains additional Hit Points equal to your Healer level + your Wisdom modifier. This additional healing is applied after the spell's normal healing has been determined.
Be aware that Gift of Healing can apply only once per spell, regardless of how many creatures the spell affects. It does not apply when you are the only target of the spell.
sections.HEALER'S TOUCH:
CONCENTRATE ESSENCE FOCUS HEALING
Action R
Trigger You or an ally within 10 feet regain Hit Points from a healing spell you cast.
All targets regain additional HP equal to the amount of PP required to cast the spell (or your level in the case of an innate spell).
sections.RESTORATIVE HANDS:
CONCENTRATE ESSENCE HEALING
Action 0 AP (Free)
Trigger You or an ally within 10 feet regain Hit Points from a healing spell you cast.
You can reduce a condition that is affecting one of the targets of the spell by one. The exact condition affected is based upon the amount of PP that is required to cast the spell:
PP 2 reduce the fatigued or sickened condition.
PP 4 reduce the dazed or weakened condition.
PP 6 reduce the injured condition.
PP 8 reduce the soul drain condition by 5.
PP 10 reduce the doomed condition by 1.
Be aware that a target may only benefit from this ability once per day.
sections.LIFELINE:
DIVINITY FOCUS HEALING SOUL
Action R
Trigger A living ally within 30 feet would gain the Dying condition because damage reduced them to 0 HP.
You instinctively seize the creature's fading life before it slips beyond your reach. The triggering creature instead remains at 1 HP and does not gain the Dying condition from the triggering damage. The creature gains Fatigued 1 from the tremendous strain placed upon its body.
Persistent damage, Bleed and other ongoing effects caused by the triggering attack are not removed.
Lifeline cannot prevent an effect that kills the target outright.
sections.RESTORATIVE OVERFLOW:
At 3rd level, your healing can reinforce a creature whose wounds have already closed. When the creature selected for Gift of Healing reaches its maximum Hit Points and some of the triggering healing would be wasted, that creature instead gains temporary Hit Points equal to the unused healing, to a maximum of your Healer level + your Wisdom modifier. These temporary Hit Points last for 1 minute.
Be aware, temporary Hit Points from Restorative Overflow do not stack with themselves; use the greater value.
sections.SPECIALIST SPELLS: At 1st level, you gain Touch of Healing as a Specialist Spell. You may learn additional spells with the Healer trait through the Specialist Spell feat and Healer class feats presented in Chapter 5.
sections.BONUS FEATS: At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, you gain an additional class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or possess the appropriate Healer or Adept class trait for the selected feat. You therefore gain bonus class feats at 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level.
sections.MAGICAL TRADITION:
You are a Divinity instinctive spellcaster. You do not memorise spells or maintain a prayer book. Your magic manifests instinctively in response to need, refined through experience rather than formal preparation.
At 1st level, you automatically add Cure and Restoration to your repertoire. These spells do not count against the normal number of spells you learn through your class.
You also select two additional PP 2 Divinity spells and add them to your repertoire.
At 2nd level and every level, thereafter, select one additional Divinity spell that you are capable of casting and add it to your repertoire. You may cast any spell in your repertoire whenever you meet its casting requirements and possess sufficient PP. You do not need to memorise spells during daily preparation.
Beginning at 5th level, whenever you gain a Healer level you may also replace one spell in your repertoire with another Divinity spell that you are capable of casting.
sections.CANTRIPS: At 1st level, you automatically learn Stabilise. You also learn two additional Divinity cantrips of your choice. These cantrips are instinctive and do not need to be memorised.
sections.MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE: Charisma is your magical ability score. You add your Wisdom modifier to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your Power Points. Your magic remains part of the Divinity tradition regardless of whether you personally worship a deity.
sections.CONTROL LEVELS: For the purposes of determining Control Levels, you gain +1 Control Level per Healer level.
sections.HEALER'S CALLING:
No two Healers approach suffering in quite the same way. At 1st level, select a Healer's Calling representing the form of healing toward which your instincts and training are most strongly drawn. Your Calling grants you a Specialist Skill and a unique ability.
The available Callings are Chirurgeon, Lifebinder, Purifier, Soul Tender and Sanctuary Keeper.
sections.CHIRURGEON:
You believe supernatural healing should supplement competent medicine rather than replace it. Chirurgeons understand anatomy, blood loss, infection, broken bones and the practical realities of keeping somebody alive when magic is unavailable.
Specialist Skill Chirurgery
Rapid Care: When you use Treat Wounds, the action takes 1 minute rather than 10 minutes. You also gain a +2-circumstance bonus to Medicine checks made to Administer First Aid or Treat Wounds. The target retains the normal temporary immunity to Treat Wounds.
sections.LIFEBINDER:
Your gift manifests as raw vitality flowing from you into damaged flesh. Some Lifebinders describe seeing a wounded creature as a pattern of light filled with broken threads. Others experience nothing more supernatural than absolute certainty about where life is slipping away.
Specialist Skill Vitality Lore
Vital Surge: Once per round, when Gift of Healing applies to a creature, you may maximise the result of one healing die rolled by the triggering spell. If the spell restores only a fixed amount of Hit Points and rolls no healing dice, this ability has no additional effect.
sections.PURIFIER:
Your gift is particularly sensitive to things that should not be within the body. Poison, disease, corruption and magical afflictions feel discordant to you, as though the patient's life is trying to reject something it cannot remove unaided.
Specialist Skill Affliction Lore
Cleansing Hands: You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to Counteract checks made to remove disease, poison or curses using a spell with the Healing trait. When you successfully Counteract such an affliction, the target also gains a +2-circumstance bonus to its next saving throw against that same affliction if some part of it remains active.
sections.SOUL TENDER:
Bodies are not the only things that can be wounded. Soul Tenders specialise in the injuries left by possession, necromancy, Soul Drain and supernatural effects that damage the animating essence of a creature.
Specialist Skill Soul Lore
Mend The Spirit: Whenever one of your spells with the Healing trait restores or removes Soul Drain, increase the amount of Soul Drain removed by 5. You also gain a +2-circumstance bonus to Counteract checks made to end possession or another effect directly controlling or displacing a creature's soul.
sections.SANCTUARY KEEPER:
You believe that healing begins before the injury occurs. Sanctuary Keepers instinctively surround those in their care with brief protective currents, using restored vitality to reinforce the body against the next attack.
Specialist Skill Hospice Lore
Sheltering Care: Whenever you select a creature to receive the additional healing from Gift of Healing, that creature also gains a +2-status bonus to DB until the beginning of your next turn.

sections.DESCRIPTION:
The world is considerably more crowded than most people realise.
An ancient oak remembers every axe laid against its bark. A river knows the shape of the valley before roads divided it. Hearths acquire personalities after generations of families gather around them. Battlefields retain grief long after the bones have been removed, and the dead sometimes leave fragments of themselves in the places, people and traditions that mattered to them.
You have learned to listen.
You are a Shaman, a spiritual intermediary whose magic emerges through relationships with the unseen presences woven throughout the living world. Some of these beings possess names and personalities. Others are little more than instinct, memory or the accumulated character of a place. An ancestor may speak in recognisable words while a mountain spirit communicates through falling stones, weather and dreams.
Your relationship with these beings is not worship. You may revere them, argue with them, negotiate with them or consider them members of an extended spiritual community. Spirits are not automatically gods, and a spirit does not become benevolent merely because it is old.
Unlike a Druid, you do not memorise spells through formal communion with nature. Verdant magic comes to you instinctively through the relationships you have formed. You know fewer spells than a Druid, but you can use them whenever required and may ask your Spirit Guide for knowledge you do not normally possess.
Every Shaman develops a particularly strong relationship with a Spirit Guide. This may be an ancestor, animal spirit, elemental presence, consciousness of the land or strange entity standing close to the veil between life and death. Your guide advises you, argues with you and occasionally acts through you.
Some cultures train Shamans formally. Others discover them when a child begins answering questions nobody else can hear.
The Myrathi are particularly renowned for producing Shamans because their Ancestral Blooms preserve fragments of memory and personality across generations, but the class belongs to no single race or culture.
You may want to play a Shaman if you enjoy instinctive Verdant magic, spiritual communication, flexible spellcasting and calling upon an otherworldly companion for supernatural abilities.
A priest asks the gods for an answer. A Shaman first asks who else is listening.
sections.PROFICIENCIES:
You are proficient with light armour and shields, except tower shields. You are proficient with all simple weapons, as well as the spear and shortbow.
Unlike a Druid, you have no prohibition against metal equipment. A Shaman's power is based upon spiritual relationships rather than adherence to the Druidic Code.
sections.CLASS SKILLS: Artistry, Culture, Diplomacy, Handle Animal, Linguistics, Medicine, Meditation, Mental Focus, Nature, Occultism, Perception, Power Manipulation, Religion, Sense Motive and Survival.
sections.CLASS ABILITIES: You gain the following abilities as a Shaman as you advance in levels.
sections.SPIRIT SPEAKER:
You perceive the world as something inhabited rather than empty.
You gain Spirit Lore as a specialist skill.
You may use Nature instead of Occultism when attempting checks to identify, understand or interact with spirits, haunts, possession and other phenomena specifically involving the spirit world.
Furthermore, you can communicate with a willing spirit within 30 feet, even where ordinary language would be insufficient, provided that the spirit possesses sufficient awareness to communicate at all.
This ability does not compel a spirit to answer you, make it friendly or grant intelligence to an otherwise mindless entity.
You also do not automatically recognise every Undead or incorporeal creature as a spirit. Spirits, souls, haunts, Undead and Unliving creatures are distinct; the individual creature or effect determines what it actually is.
sections.SPIRIT COMMUNION:
Your relationship with the unseen world allows you to acquire magic that does not normally form part of your repertoire.
During your daily preparation you commune with your Spirit Guide.
At the end of this communion, select one PP 2 Ethereal spell. You temporarily add that spell to your repertoire.
The spell remains in your repertoire until your next daily preparation, at which point the knowledge fades.
At 6th level, you may use Spirit Communion to add two spells with a maximum PP of 4. At 12th level three spells with a maximum PP of 10 and at 18th level 4 spells with a maximum PP of 14.
sections.SPIRIT WARD:
At 3rd level, constant exposure to spiritual influence has made your own soul unusually difficult to disturb.
You gain a +2-class bonus to saving throws against possession, Soul Drain and effects with the Soul trait.
Furthermore, whenever you successfully resist possession, you immediately become aware that something attempted to enter or control you, even if the original effect would normally conceal that information.
sections.DEEPENED BOND:
At 7th level, your Spirit Guide can remain closer to the physical world.
Whenever you successfully Refocus an expended Shaman Focus ability, you may choose Manifest Spirit or Spirit Intercession and restore that ability in addition to the ability you were attempting to restore.
You cannot restore the same ability twice.
sections.BONUS FEATS:
At 1st level, you gain Heighten Spell as a bonus feat.
At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter, you gain an additional class feat. You must meet its prerequisites or possess the appropriate Shaman or Adept trait.
You therefore gain bonus class feats at 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level.
sections.MAGICAL TRADITION:
You are a full instinctive Verdant spellcaster.
Unlike a Druid, you do not memorise Verdant spells during daily preparation. Your repertoire represents magical workings taught by spirits so thoroughly that you can invoke them instinctively.
At 1st level, select two PP 2 Verdant spells and add them to your repertoire. At 2nd level and every level, thereafter, select one additional Verdant spell that you are capable of casting and add it to your repertoire.
You may cast any spell within your repertoire whenever you meet its casting requirements and possess sufficient PP.
Beginning at 5th level, whenever you gain a Shaman level, you may replace one spell in your repertoire with another Verdant spell that you are capable of casting.
sections.CANTRIPS:
At 1st level, select three Verdant cantrips. These become part of your permanent repertoire and do not need to be memorised.
Any bonus cantrip granted by your Spirit Guide is additional to these three.
sections.MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE:
Constitution is your magical ability score.
You add your Constitution modifier to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your Power Points.
Your magic remains part of the Verdant tradition.
sections.SPECIALIST SPELLS:
At 1st level, you gain one PP 1 Shaman Specialist Spell of your choice.
Shaman Specialist Spells will be presented in the Grimoire and concentrate on direct dealings with spirits rather than duplicating Druid magic.
Additional Shaman Specialist Spells may be learned through the normal Specialist Spell feat and Shaman class feats.
sections.CONTROL LEVELS: For the purpose of determining Control Levels, you gain +1 Control Level per Shaman level.
sections.MANIFEST SPIRIT:
CONCENTRATE FOCUS SPIRIT
Action 1 AP
Duration 1 minute
You allow your Spirit Guide to manifest more completely around and through you.
The manifestation may appear as spectral figures, animal features, swirling leaves, elemental light, ancestral voices or another effect appropriate to your guide.
You gain the Manifestation ability associated with your Spirit Guide for the duration.
You may dismiss the manifestation as a Free (0 AP) action.
sections.SPIRIT INTERCESSION:
CHANCE CONCENTRATE FOCUS SPIRIT
Action R; Trigger you fail a saving throw
Your Spirit Guide warns, shields or momentarily strengthens you.
Reroll the triggering saving throw and use the better result.
Spirit Intercession is then expended and must be restored through Refocus.
At 7th level, you may also use Spirit Intercession when an ally within 30 feet fails a saving throw. The ally must be capable of benefiting from your Spirit Guide's intervention; Line of Effect is required.
sections.ANCESTOR SPIRIT:
Your guide is the surviving presence of someone who lived before you.
It might genuinely be one of your ancestors, but blood relationship is unnecessary. Some spirits adopt descendants, apprentices, communities or even complete strangers whose lives somehow continue their unfinished work.
Specialist Skill Ancestor Lore
Spirit Boon - Borrowed Memory: You gain a +1-class bonus to Recall Knowledge checks. Once per day, when you attempt a Recall Knowledge check using a skill in which you have no ranks, you may treat yourself as having 1 rank in that skill for the purposes of the check. The ancestor does not automatically possess information that could never reasonably have been known to them.
Manifestation - Chorus Of The Past: While Manifest Spirit is active, you gain Advantage on Recall Knowledge and Sense Motive checks and a +1-circumstance bonus to Will saving throws.
At times, several indistinct ancestral voices may be heard answering alongside your own.
sections.BEAST SPIRIT:
Your Spirit Guide embodies the instinctive qualities of an animal or collection of animals.
It need not correspond to a literal animal that once lived. A wolf spirit might represent pack loyalty and pursuit rather than the soul of a particular wolf.
Specialist Skill Animal Lore
Spirit Boon – Wild Understanding: You may communicate with animals on a rudimentary level through posture, emotion, sound and spiritual intuition.
You gain a +2-class bonus to checks made to communicate with animals.
Manifestation – Beast Within: While Manifest Spirit is active:
• your Speed increases by 10 feet;
• you gain Scent as a tertiary sense; and
• you gain a +1-dodge bonus to DB.
Spectral claws, antlers, feathers, scales, eyes or other features of your Spirit Guide may become visible around your body.
sections.ELEMENTAL SPIRIT:
You are guided by one of the fundamental forces expressed within the natural world.
When selecting this guide, choose Acid, Cold, Electricity or Fire. This choice cannot normally be changed.
Specialist Skill Elemental Lore
Spirit Boon - Elemental: You gain a +1-class bonus to saving throws against effects possessing your selected elemental trait.
You also add an appropriate Verdant cantrip possessing that elemental trait to your repertoire. This is a bonus cantrip and does not count against your normal cantrips known.
Manifestation – Elemental Mantle: While Manifest Spirit is active, you gain Resistance to your selected damage type.
Furthermore, once per round when one of your Verdant spells inflicts damage of your selected type, one target damaged by that spell suffers an additional 1d6 secondary damage of the same type.
This damage increases to 2d6 at 9th level and 3d6 at 17th level.
sections.LAND SPIRIT:
Your guide is bound to the character of a place: a mountain, ancient woodland, river valley, cave system, desert, marsh or other enduring landscape.
You may have inherited the bond from generations of Shamans, or the place itself may simply have decided that you were worth following.
Specialist Skill Select one appropriate Terrain Lore skill.
Spirit Boon – Memory of the Land: You gain a +2-class bonus to Nature and Survival checks involving the terrain represented by your Spirit Guide.
Furthermore, you ignore natural difficult terrain of that type.
Manifestation – Rooted World: While Manifest Spirit is active:
• your Base DR increases by 1;
• you gain Advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being Shoved, Tripped or moved against your will; and
• you ignore ordinary natural difficult terrain.
Earth may harden beneath your feet; roots may briefly coil around your legs or fragments of the landscape represented by your guide may appear around you.
sections.VEIL SPIRIT:
Your guide exists close to the uncertain boundary between embodied life and the unseen world.
It may be a departed ancestor, a spirit that never possessed a mortal body or something whose true nature remains unclear even to you.
Specialist Skill Veil Lore.
Spirit Boon – Second Sight: You gain Spirit Sense as a tertiary sense.
When using Search (Perception), you can detect the presence and general direction of disembodied spirits, incorporeal undead, haunts and active possession within 30 feet.
You cannot determine exact location, identity or allegiance from Spirit Sense alone.
Manifestation – Part the Veil: While Manifest Spirit is active:
• the range of your Spirit Sense increases to 60 feet;
• you gain Resistance to essence damage;
• you can perceive spirits detected by Spirit Sense sufficiently clearly to target them, provided they are otherwise within range and Line of Effect; and
• your spells treat incorporeal spirits as though you possessed the normal means required to affect them.
This ability does not allow a spell to affect a creature that would otherwise be completely immune to that spell for reasons unrelated to incorporeality.
